result.topic_en: Euler gives the series Q and Q' and says the critical value of t must be found by trial from P + PQ' − QP' = 0. He then calibrates the elastic constant against a test column of the same material, giving the critical height b in fully known quantities.

$Q' = \frac{1 \cdot t}{2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4} - \frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot t^2}{2 \ldots 7} + \frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 6 \cdot t^3}{1 \ldots\ldots 10} - \text{etc.}$

§. 31. Postquam autem hinc verus valor numeri
$t$ fuerit erutus, vt inde statim quaesitam altitudinem $b$
in mensura penitus cognita assignare valeamus, ponamus
haberi columnam cylindricam, ex eadem materia paratam,
cuius altitudo sit $= a$, amplitudo vero $= d d$, et quae
per experimenta comperta sit gestare posse onus $\Gamma$, quod
se habeat ad pondus huius columnae, vt $\lambda : 1$, ita vt sit
$\Gamma = \lambda\, a d d$. Iam ex iis, quae de vi columnarum iam
olim sunt tradita, istud onus $\Gamma$ inuentum est
$\Gamma = \frac{\pi \pi E k k}{a a}$,
existente $E k k = d^4 e$, vnde ergo fiet
$e = \frac{\Gamma . a a}{\pi \pi d^4} = \frac{\lambda a^3}{\pi \pi d d}$.
Substituatur ergo iste valor in formula nostra pro $b$ in-
uenta, ac reperietur
$b = a \sqrt[3]{\frac{\lambda b b}{\pi \pi d d}}$.
vbi iam omnia elementa penitus sunt cognita.

Calculus

items.quote: atque nunc totum negotium huc redit, vt ille valor ipsius $t$ inuestigetur, quo huic aequationi satisfiat: $P + P Q'$ $- Q P' = 0$, id quod aliter nisi tentando fieri nequit: plures scilicet pro $t$ assumi conueniet successiue valores, atque ex erroribus singulorum concludi poterit verus valor ipsius $t$.
items.english: And now the whole business comes down to finding the value of t that satisfies the equation P + PQ' − QP' = 0. This can only be done by trial: several values of t should be assumed in succession, and from the errors of each the true value of t can be inferred.

items.quote: Mox autem inuestiganti patebit, valorem ipsius $t$ non exiguum esse, sed potius satis magnum accipi debere.
items.english: But it will soon become clear to the investigator that the value of t is not small, but rather must be taken fairly large.

items.quote: vt inde statim quaesitam altitudinem $b$ in mensura penitus cognita assignare valeamus
items.english: so that from it we may at once assign the sought height b in a fully known measure
